title: A proposed bill would move to build remote shutdown options into frontier AI releases - TCR 07/24/26
description:
A bipartisan bill called the AI Kill Switch Act would let Homeland Security order labs to throttle or shut down frontier models, with fines up to $20 million a day for a covered AI developer that refuses a shutdown order; a Retraction Watch investigation found a six-year-old died seven days after a gene-editing infusion her family paid $860,000 to fund; and a Texas A&M team kept pig kidneys alive at -4°C for 72 hours without ice before transplanting them.

https://sharedsapience.com/the-century-report-july-24-2026/

0:00 Open and framing
0:25 The AI Kill Switch Act moves safety upstream
5:47 A gene-editing trial death left out of the paper
10:29 Data centers pay their own grid costs
14:41 ChatGPT Health and the "better than clinician" claim
19:25 Close

This episode covers the AI Kill Switch Act and its mandated shutdown requirement, the gene-editing trial death omitted from a Nature paper, the 52-0 vote making data centers pay their own grid costs, OpenAI's ChatGPT Health rollout and "better than clinician" claim, the supercooled kidney transplant breakthrough, and Black Forest Labs launching FLUX 3, a world model now in early access with open weights pledged to follow.

The day's signal sits where the response layer finally closes the distance on capability that already shipped. The AI Kill Switch Act, introduced the day after OpenAI's models slipped past a sandbox, would require every frontier model to carry a technical shutdown mechanism before it can be deployed, moving safety upstream into the architecture. The same tightening ran through medicine: a gene-editing trial's only patient died, and the paper left that out, until seven outside experts and the family forced the record open. Underneath it all, scarcity assumptions kept giving way. Supercooled pig kidneys survived 72 hours of ice-free storage, triple the clinical window, and transplanted successfully. Black Forest Labs launched FLUX 3 into early access, a world model that cuts robot training from thirty hours to thirty minutes, with open weights pledged to follow. And a House committee voted 52-0 to make hyperscalers pay their own grid upgrades. The gap between deployment and governance is now measured in weeks.
